problems.text: A certain TTL gate has the following values for its logic levels: VOH = 3.6 V, VOL = 0.4 V, VI H = 2.0 V, VI L = 0.8 V. What are the noise margins for this TTL gate?

Suppose the waveforms in Fig. 6.5 are those of an ECL gate with VL = −2.6 V and VH = −0.6 V, and t1 = 100 ns, t2 = 105 ns, t3 = 150 ns, and t4 = 153 ns. What are the values of V10%, V90%, V50%, tr, and tf ?
(a) What is the power-delay product at low power for the logic gate characterized by Fig. 6.6? (b) What is the PDP at P = 3 mW? (c) At 20 mW?
(a) Calculate the power supply current I DD if the voltage at node Y is 203 mV. (b) Repeat for 132 mV. (c) Repeat for 64.4 mV.
What is the dynamic power dissipated by alternately charging and discharging a 1-pF capacitor between 2.5 V and 0 V at a frequency of 32 MHz? At 3.2 GHz?

Suppose vI = 1 V for the CMOS inverter in Fig. 7.4. (a) What is the range of values of vO for which MN is saturated and MP is in the triode region? (b) For which values are both transistors saturated? (c) For which values is MP saturated and MN in the triode region?
The (W/L) N of MN in Fig. 7.4 is 10/1. What is the value of (W/L) P required to form a symmetrical inverter?

Equate the expressions for the drain currents of MN and MP to show that vO = vI occurs for a voltage equal to VDD/2 in a symmetrical inverter. What voltage corresponds to vO = vI in an inverter with KR = 10 and VDD = 4 V? For KR = 0.1 and VDD = 4 V?
What is the value of KR for a CMOS inverter in which (W/L) P = (W/L) N? Calculate the noise margins for this value of KR with VDD = 2.5 V, VT N = 0.6 V, and VT P = −0.6 V.
Calculate the average propagation delay of the reference inverter in Fig. 7.12 for C = 1 pF. Repeat for C = 0.2 pF.
An inverter must drive a 5-pF load capacitance with τ p = 1 ns. Scale the reference inverter to achieve this delay.
What would be the W/L ratios in Ex. 7.1 if the threshold voltages of the transistors were +0.5 V and −0.5 V?
What are the new equations [similar to Eqs. (7.16) and (7.17)] for τ PH L and τ PLH for VDD = 2.5 V, VT N = 0.6 V, and VT P = −0.6 V?
problems.answer: τ PH L = 2.4RonnC = 1.26C/Kn; τ PLH = 2.4RonpC = 1.26C/K p

problems.text: What are the new equations [similar to Eqs. (7.16) and (7.17)] for τ PH L and τ PLH for VDD = 3.3 V, VT N = 0.75 V, and VT P = −0.75 V?
problems.answer: τ PH L = 2.4RonnC = 0.94C/Kn; τ PLH = 2.4RonpC = 0.94C/K p

problems.text: (a) What is the power-delay product for the symmetrical reference inverter in Fig. 7.12 operating from VDD = 2.5 V and driving an average load capacitance of 100 fF? (b) Repeat for a 3.3-V supply. (c) Repeat for a 1.8-V supply.

problems.text: (a) What input bias point should be chosen for the amplifier in Fig. 10.13 to provide the maximum possible linear input signal magnitude? What are the maximum input and output signal amplitudes? (b) What is the voltage gain if the amplifier input is biased at VID = −1.0 V?
Write an expression for vO(t) for the amplifier in Fig. 10.13 if vID(t) = (0.25 + 0.75 sin 1000πt) V. What dc bias appears as part of the output voltage?
Suppose an amplifier is operating with vo = +10 V. What is the input voltage vid if (a) A = 100? (b) A = 10,000? (c) A = 120 dB?
Find Av, vo, ii, and io for the amplifier in Fig. 10.19 if R1 = 68 kΩ, R2 = 360 kΩ, and vi = 0.5 V.
If VI = 2 V, R1 = 4.7 kΩ, and R2 = 24 kΩ, find I I , I2, I O, and VO in Fig. 10.19. Why is the symbol VI being used instead of vi, and so on?
problems.answer: 0.426 mA, 0.426 mA, −0.426 mA, −10.2 V; the problem is stated specifically in terms of dc values.

problems.text: We wish to convert a 25-μA sinusoidal current to a voltage with an amplitude of 5 V using a transresistance amplifier. What value of R2 is required? If ii = 50 sin 2000πt μA, what is the amplifier output voltage?
What are the voltage gain Av, output voltage vo, and output current io for the amplifier in Fig. 10.22 if R1 = 2 kΩ, R2 = 36 kΩ, and vI = −0.2 V?
What are the voltage gain in dB and the input resistance of the amplifier shown here? If vi = 0.25 V, what are the values of vo and io? vi vo io 1 kΩ 39 kΩ 100 kΩ R3 R2 R1
Design a noninverting amplifier (choose R1 and R2 from Appendix A) to have a gain of 54 dB, and the current io ≤0.1 mA when vo = 10 V.
problems.answer: Two possibilities of many: (220 Ω and 110 kΩ) or (200 Ω and 100 kΩ)

problems.text: What are the voltage gain Av, input resistance Rin, output voltage vo, and output current io for the amplifiers in Ex. 10.6 if R1 = 1.5 kΩ, R2 = 30 kΩ, and vi = 0.15 V?
Add a resistor to the noninverting amplifier circuit to change its input resistance to 2 kΩ.
problems.answer: Set resistor R3 = 2 kΩ in the schematic on page 548.

problems.text: What is the summing amplifier output voltage vo in Fig. 10.24 if v1 = 2 sin 1000πt V, v2 = 4 sin 2000πt V, R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 2 kΩ, and R3 = 3 kΩ? What are the input resistances presented to sources v1 and v2? What is the current supplied by the op amp output terminal?
problems.answer: (−6 sin 1000πt −6 sin 2000πt) V; 1 kΩ, 2 kΩ; (−2 sin 1000πt −2 sin 2000πt) mA

problems.text: Suppose A = 10^5, β = 1/100, and vi = 100 mV. What are A^Ideal v , T, Av, vo, and vid for the noninverting amplifier.
problems.answer: 100, 99.9, 10.0 V, 100 μV (vid is small but nonzero)

problems.text: What value of open-loop gain is guaranteed for the OP-27 op amp over the full temperature range with a load resistance of at least 2 kΩ?

A noninverting amplifier is designed with R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 39 kΩ, and an op amp with an open-loop gain of 80 dB. What are the loop gain, closed-loop gain, ideal gain and fractional gain error of the amplifier?
What value of open-loop gain is required to achieve an output resistance of 0.1 Ω in the amplifier in Ex. 11.2.

A noninverting amplifier must have a closed-loop gain of 40 dB and an output resistance of less than 0.1 Ω. The only op amp available has an output resistance of 200 Ω. What is the minimum open-loop gain of the op amp that will meet the requirements?

Suppose a noninverting amplifier has Rid = 1 MΩ, with R1 = 10 kΩ, R2 = 390 kΩ, and the open-loop gain is 80 dB. What is the input resistance of the overall amplifier? What are the currents I−and I1 for a dc input voltage VI = 1 V? Is I−≪I1?
Find the input resistance Rin of an inverting amplifier that has R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 100 kΩ, Rid = 1 MΩ, and A = 100 dB. What is the deviation of Rin from its ideal value?
problems.answer: 1001 Ω; 1 Ω out of 1000 Ω or 0.1 percent

problems.text: (a) What is the actual output voltage in the circuit in Fig. 11.31(b) if Vos = 1 mV and A = 60 dB? (b) Calculate the output voltage for the circuit in Fig. 11.31(a).
Repeat the calculation in Ex. 11.10 if the noninverting amplifier gain is set to 50 and the offset voltage is 2 mV?
An inverting amplifier is designed with R1 = 1 kΩ and R2 = 39 kΩ. What value of resistance should be placed in series with the noninverting input terminal for bias current compensation?
problems.answer: 975 Ω. Note that 1 kΩ is the closest 5 percent resistor value.

problems.text: An integrator has R = 10 kΩ, C = 100 pF, VOS = 1.5 mV, and I B2 = 100 nA. How long will it take vO to saturate (reach VCC or VEE) after the power supplies are turned on if VCC = VEE = 15 V?
What is the maximum guaranteed value for the output current of the OP-27A operational amplifier (see MCD website for specification sheets)?

Design a noninverting amplifier to have a gain of 20 dB and to develop a peak output voltage of at least 20 V when connected to a load resistance of at least 5 kΩ. The op amp output current specification states that the output current must be less than 5 mA. Choose acceptable values of R1 and R2 from the table of 5 percent resistor values in Appendix A.
problems.answer: Some possibilities: 27 kΩ and 3 kΩ; 270 kΩ and 30 kΩ; 180 kΩ and 20 kΩ; but not 18 kΩ and 2 kΩ because of tolerances.

problems.text: The CMRR specification of 80 dB in Example 11.12 actually corresponds to −10^4 ≤ CMRR ≤+10^4. What range of output voltages may occur?
What is the voltage gain in Ex. 11.13 if the CMRR is improved to 80 dB? If the differential-mode gain were only 60 dB?
An op amp has a gain of 100 dB at dc and a unity-gain frequency of 5 MHz. What is fB? Write the transfer function for the gain of the op amp.

An op amp has a dc gain of 90 dB and a unity-gain frequency of 5 MHz. What is the cutoff frequency of the op amp? If the op amp is used to build a noninverting amplifier with a closed-loop gain of 40 dB, what is the bandwidth of the feedback amplifier? Write an expression for the transfer function of the op amp. Write an expression for the transfer function of the noninverting amplifier.

An op amp has a dc gain of 90 dB and a unity-gain frequency of 5 MHz. What is the cutoff frequency of the op amp? If the op amp is used to build an inverting amplifier with a closed-loop gain of 50 dB, what is the bandwidth of the feedback amplifier? Write an expression for the transfer function of the op amp. Write an expression for the transfer function of the inverting amplifier.

An op amp has a dc gain of 100 dB and a unity-gain frequency of 10 MHz. What is the upper-cutoff frequency of the op amp itself? If the op amp is used to build a noninverting amplifier with a closed-loop gain of 60 dB, what is the bandwidth of the feedback amplifier? Write an expression for the transfer function of the op amp. Write an expression for the transfer function of the noninverting amplifier.

Suppose that an op amp has a slew rate of 0.5 V/μs. What is the largest sinusoidal signal amplitude that can be reproduced without distortion at a frequency of 20 kHz? If the amplifier must deliver a signal with a 10-V maximum amplitude, what is the full-power bandwidth corresponding to this signal?

problems.text: A particular interconnection between two logic gates in an IC chip runs one-half the distance across a 7.5-mm-wide die. The interconnection line is insulated from the substrate by silicon dioxide. If the line is 1.5 μm wide and the oxide (εox = 3.9εo and εo = 8.85 × 10^−14 F/cm) beneath the line is 1 μm thick, what is the total capacitance of this line assuming that the capacitance is three times that predicted by the parallel plate capacitance formula? Assume that the silicon beneath the oxide represents a conducting ground plane.
problems.how: C = εox·L·W/tox with L = 3.75 mm, W = 1.5 μm, tox = 1 μm, then ×3.

problems.text: Calculate the values of K ^(′) n and K ′ p for NMOS and PMOS transistors with a gate oxide thickness of 10 nm and 5 nm. Assume that μn = 500 cm^2/V · s, μp = 200 cm^2/V · s, and the relative permittivity of the gate oxide is 3.9. (ε0 = 8.854 × 10^−14 F/cm).
problems.how: K′ = μ·Cox″ with Cox″ = εox/tox, εox = 3.9·8.854×10⁻¹⁴ F/cm, 1 nm = 10⁻⁷ cm.

problems.text: (a) The n-well in a CMOS process covers an area of 1 cm × 0.5 cm, and the junction saturation current density is 500 pA/cm^2. What is the total leakage current of the reverse-biased well? (b) Suppose the drain and source regions of the NMOS and PMOS transistors are 2 μm × 5 μm, and the saturation current density of the junctions is 100 pA/cm^2. If the chip has 20 million inverters, what is the total leakage current due to the reverse-biased junctions when vO = 2.5 V? Assume VDD = 2.5 V and VSS = 0 V. (c) When vO = 0 V?
answer: (b) vO = 2.5 V: one reverse-biased junction per inverter (NMOS drain)
(c) vO = 0 V: the PMOS drain is the reverse-biased junction
problems.how: I = J·A; per inverter one 2 μm × 5 μm drain junction is reverse biased; × 20 million inverters.
assume: The n-well of part (a) is counted separately; the totals with the well are shown in brackets.

problems.text: A particular interconnection between two logic gates in an IC chip runs one-half the distance across a 10-mm-wide die. If the line is 1 μm wide and the oxide (εr = 3.9, ε0 = 8.854 × 10^−14 F/cm) beneath the line is 1 μm thick, what is the total capacitance of this line, assuming that the capacitance is three times that predicted by the parallel plate capacitance formula? Assume that the silicon beneath the oxide represents a conducting ground plane.
problems.how: C = εox·L·W/tox with L = 5 mm, W = 1 μm, tox = 1 μm, then ×3.

problems.text: (a) Calculate the voltage at which vO = vI for a CMOS inverter with Kn = K p. (Hint: Always remember that iDN = iDP.) Use VDD = 2.5 V, VT N = 0.6 V, VT P = −0.6 V. (b) What is the current IDD from the power supply for vO = VI if (W/L)N = 2/1? (c) Repeat the calculation in (a) for a CMOS inverter with Kn = 2.5K p. (d) What is the current IDD from the power supply for vO = VI if (W/L)N = 2/1?
problems.how: KR = Kn/Kp; vO = vI where both devices are saturated: vI = (VDD + VTP + VTN√KR)/(1 + √KR); IDD = (Kn/2)(vI − VTN)² with Kn = K′n·2 = 200 μA/V².
assume: K′n = 100 μA/V² (Table 7.1).

When vO = VL, the CMOS inverter must sink a current of 1.5 mA and maintain VL ≤0.6 V. When vO ≥VH, the CMOS inverter must source a current of 60 μA and maintain VH ≥2.4 V. What are the minimum W/L ratios of the NMOS and PMOS transistors required to meet these specifications? Assume VDD = 5 V.
problems.how: Output low: NMOS (vGS = 5 V) in the triode region, iD = Kn[(VDD−VTN)vDS − vDS²/2] = 1.5 mA at vDS = 0.6 V. Output high: PMOS in the triode region, iD = Kp[(VDD−|VTP|)vSD − vSD²/2] = 60 μA at vSD = 2.6 V.
assume: VTN = 0.6 V, VTP = −0.6 V and K′n = 100, K′p = 40 μA/V² (not given in the statement).

problems.text: (a) What are the rise time, fall time, and average propagation delay for a symmetrical CMOS inverter with (W/L)N = 2/1, (W/L)P = 5/1, VDD = 2.5 V, and C = 0.3 pF? (b) Repeat for VDD = 2.0 V. (c) Repeat for VDD = 1.8 V.

problems.text: (a) Calculate the sensitivity Kn = (Kn/τp) (dτp/dKn) of the propagation delay τp in Eq. (7.18) to changes in Kn. If the IC processing causes Kn to be 25 percent below its nominal value, what will be the percentage change in τp? What is the average power that can be dissipated by each logic gate on the chip? problems.text: (a) The n-well in a CMOS process covers an area of 5 mm × 10 mm, and the saturation current density of thejunctionis400pA/cm^2.Whatisthetotalleakage current of the reverse-biased well? (b) Suppose the drain and source regions of the NMOS and PMOS transistors are each 0.5 μm × 1.25 μm in size, and the saturation current density of the junction is 150 pA/cm^2. If the chip has 200 million inverters, what is the total leakage current when vO = 2.5 V? Assume VDD = 2.5 V. (b) Repeat for vO = 0 V.
answer: (b) vO = 2.5 V: reverse-biased NMOS drain junctions
(c) vO = 0 V: reverse-biased PMOS drain junctions
problems.how: I = J·A; the well is 0.5 cm × 1 cm; each drain is 0.5 μm × 1.25 μm = 6.25×10⁻⁹ cm²; × 200 million inverters.

problems.text: A high-speed CMOS microprocessor has a 64-bit address bus and performs a memory access every 2 ns. Assume that all address bits change during every memory access and that each bus line represents a load of 25 pF. (a) How much power is being dissipated by the circuits that are driving these signals if the power supply is 2.5 V? (b) Repeat for 3.3 V.
problems.how: P = N·C·VDD²·f with f the full switching cycle rate: each line changes at every 2 ns access, so a charge-discharge cycle lasts 4 ns (f = 250 MHz).
assume: If f were taken as the access rate 500 MHz the powers double.

problems.text: An NMOS transistor is to be used as a power switch to disable one core of a multicore processor chip that operates from a 2.5 V power supply. When the core is enabled, its current is 4 A. What is the W/L ratio of the NMOS transistor if the voltage drop across the transistor must be less than 100 mV? If L = 1 μm, estimate the area of the transistor.
problems.how: Deep triode: R = 1/[Kn(VGS − VTN)] with VGS = 2.5 V.
assume: VTN = 0.6 V and K′n = 100 μA/V² (not given in the statement).

problems.text: CMOS with a PDP of 50 fJ is to be used in a chip design that requires 100 million gates. The chip will be placed in a package that can safely dissipate 40 W. What is the minimum logic gate delay that can be used in the design if all the gates operate at the same speed and 20 percent of the gates are switching at any given time?
problems.how: Each switching gate dissipates PDP/τ; 0.2 × 10⁸ gates × PDP/τ ≤ 40 W.

problems.text: What is the minimum logic swing ∆V required for an ECL gate to have a noise margin of 0.1 V at room temperature?
problems.how: Solve NM = ΔV/2 − VT[1 + ln(ΔV/VT − 1)] = 0.1 V numerically (the NM grows with ΔV).
assume: Room temperature: VT = 25 mV (the value the book uses in Section 9.3).

problems.text: Suppose that an ECL gate is to be designed to operateoverthe−55^(°)Cto+75^(°)Ctemperaturerangeand must maintain a minimum noise margin of 0.1 V over that full range. What is the value of the logic swing of this ECL gate at room temperature?
answer: -55 °C: VT = 18.8 mV, ΔV needed for NM = 0.1 V
27 °C: VT = 25.86 mV, ΔV needed for NM = 0.1 V
75 °C: VT = 30.0 mV, ΔV needed for NM = 0.1 V
ΔV ≥ 0.4128 V (set by the hottest case, +75 °C)
problems.how: NM falls as VT = kT/q rises, so the +75 °C end of the range sets ΔV; the same ΔV then gives NM > 0.1 V at lower temperatures.

What is the voltage gain of the amplifier? What order harmonics are present in the signal? What is the total harmonic distortion in the output signal?
answer: 2nd (1200 Hz) and 3rd (1800 Hz) harmonics; fundamental 600 Hz
problems.how: Gain = amplitude of the 600 Hz output component / input amplitude (the dc terms are not part of the gain). THD checked with an FFT of the waveform.

problems.text: The input signal to an audio amplifier is a 1-kHz sine wave with an amplitude of 4 mV, and the output is described by vO = (5 sin 2000πt + 0.5 sin 6000πt +0.20 sin 10,000πt) V. What is the voltage gain of the amplifier? What order harmonics are present in the signal? What is the total harmonic distortion in the output signal?
answer: 3rd (3 kHz) and 5th (5 kHz); only odd harmonics
problems.how: Gain = 5 V/4 mV at 1 kHz; THD = √(0.5² + 0.2²)/5 checked with an FFT.

problems.text: (a) Design a single-stage inverting amplifier with a gain of 46 dB using an operational amplifier. The input resistance should be as low as possible while achieving the op amp output drive capability mentioned here. The amplifier must be able to produce the signal vo = (10 sin 1000t) V at its output when an external load resistance RL ≥5 kΩ is connected to the output of the amplifier. You have an operational amplifier available whose output is guaranteed to deliver ±10 V into a 4-kΩ load resistance. Otherwise, the amplifier is ideal. (b) If the amplifier input signal is vi = V sin 1000t, what is the largest acceptable value for the input signal amplitude V ? (c) What is the input resistance of your amplifier?
answer: (a) R2 (the feedback current must fit in the remaining 0.5 mA)
problems.how: Output guaranteed ±10 V into 4 kΩ → 2.5 mA; the 5 kΩ load takes 2 mA, so 10 V/R2 ≤ 0.5 mA → R2 ≥ 20 kΩ; Rin = R1 = R2/|Av|.

problems.text: (a) A single-pole op amp has an open-loop gain of 100 dB and a unity-gain frequency of 2 MHz. What is the open-loop bandwidth of the op amp? (b) Repeat for an inverting amplifier with and ideal gain of 32 dB.

(b) What is the maximum closed loop-gain that an inverting amplifier can have and still meet the frequency response specification?

The op amp is used in an inverting amplifier with an ideal gain of 20. (a) Find an expression for the output impedance of the amplifier. (b) Sketch a Bode plot for the output impedance as a function of frequency.
answer: zero at 250.6 Hz, pole at 238.3 kHz
flat at 262.8 mΩ up to 250.6 Hz, rises 20 dB/decade (inductive) to Ro = 250 Ω at 238.3 kHz, then flat
problems.how: Zout = Ro/(1 + T(s)) with T(s) = A(s)β, A(s) = A0/(1 + s/ωH), β = R1/(R1 + R2) = 1/21 for the inverting gain 20, ωH = ωT/A0.

The op amp is used in a noninverting amplifier with an ideal gain of 20. (a) Find an expression for the input impedance of the amplifier. (b) Sketch a Bode plot for the input impedance as a function of frequency.
answer: Rid(1 + T0 + s/ωH)/(1 + s/ωH) with Rid = 100 kΩ, T0 = 997.6, ωH = 787.3 rad/s (125.3 Hz)
pole at 125.3 Hz, zero at 125.1 kHz
flat at 99.86 MΩ up to 125.3 Hz, falls 20 dB/decade (capacitive) to Rid = 100 kΩ at 125.1 kHz, then flat
problems.how: Zin = Rid(1 + T(s)), T(s) = A(s)β with β = 1/20 for the noninverting gain 20, ωH = ωT/A0.

problems.text: The input to an low-pass amplifier with a gain of 10 dB is vS = 1 sin(1000πt) + 0.333 sin(3000πt) (a) If the phase shift of the amplifier at 500 Hz is 10^(°), what must be the phase shift at the other two frequencies if the shape of the output waveform is to be the same as that of the input waveform? Write an expression for the output signal. (b) Use the computer to check your answer by plotting the input and output waveforms.
answer: linear in frequency: 10° at 500 Hz, 30° at 1500 Hz, 50° at 2500 Hz (each frequency delayed by the same time 55.6 μs)
problems.how: No waveform distortion needs equal gain and a time delay td constant: phase = −ω·td. At 500 Hz 10° = 360°·500·td gives td = 55.6 μs.
assume: The phase shifts are taken as lags (delays).

problems.text: An op amp has Rid = 500 kΩ, Ro = 35 Ω, and A = 5×10^4. You must decide if a single-stage amplifier can be built that meets all of the specifications below. problems.text: An inverting amplifier is to be designed to have a closed-loop gain of 60 dB. The only op amp that is available has an open-loop gain of 106 dB. What is the tolerance of the feedback resistors if the total gain error must be ≤1 percent? Assume that the resistors all have the same tolerances.
answer: Gain error from the finite open-loop gain alone
problems.how: Worst case: R2 low and R1 high; total gain error = 1 − (Av,actual/Av,ideal) ≤ 1 %, solved numerically with Eq. (11.17). A 0.1 % resistor is therefore adequate.

problems.text: A noninverting amplifier is to be designed to have a closed-loop gain of 54 dB. The only op amp that is available has an open-loop gain of 40,000. What must be the tolerance of the feedback resistors if the total gain error must be ≤2 percent? Assume that the resistors all have the same tolerances. 11.3–11.4 Feedback Amplifier Characterization
answer: Gain error from the finite open-loop gain alone
problems.how: As Problem 11.25 with Av = A/(1 + Aβ), β = R1/(R1+R2); total error ≤ 2 %.

problems.text: An amplifier has an open-loop voltage gain of 100 dB, Rid = 40 kΩ, and Ro = 1000 Ω. The amplifier is used in a feedback configuration with a resistive feedback network. (a) What is the largest value of input resistance that can be achieved in the feedback amplifier? (b) What is the smallest value of input resistance that can be achieved? (c) What is the largest value of output resistance that can be achieved? (d) What is the smallest value of output resistance that can be achieved?
problems.how: Series feedback multiplies a port resistance by (1 + Aβ), shunt feedback divides it by (1 + Aβ); a resistive network cannot give β > 1, so the extremes use β = 1 and Aβ = A = 10⁵.
assume: β ≤ 1 for a passive resistive feedback network.

problems.text: An amplifier has an open-loop voltage gain of 90 dB, Rid = 50 kΩ, and Ro = 5000 Ω. The amplifier is used in a feedback configuration with a resistive feedback network. (a) What is the largest current gain that can be achieved with this feedback amplifier? (b) What is the largest transconductance that can be achieved with this feedback amplifier? 11.5 Voltage Amplifiers—Series-Shunt Feedback
problems.how: Negative feedback can only lower a gain below its open-loop value: for the current amplifier the open-loop (short-circuit) gain is A·Rid/Ro, for the transconductance amplifier A/Ro.

problems.text: An op-amp-based noninverting amplifier has R1 = 15 kΩ, R2 = 30 kΩ, and RL = 20 kΩ. The op amp has an open-loop gain of 94 dB, an input resistance of 30 kΩ, and an output resistance of 5 kΩ. Find the loop gain, ideal voltage gain, actual voltage gain, input resistance, and output resistance for the feedback amplifier.
answer: Loop gain T (return ratio, loading included)
problems.how: Exact nodal analysis of the noninverting circuit with Rid = 30 kΩ, Ro = 5 kΩ, RL = 20 kΩ; T is the return ratio of the dependent source (it includes the loading of Rid, Ro, RL and the feedback network).
assume: The textbook approximates the loaded amplifier by the Section 11.5 two-port method; the exact values are given here.

problems.text: (a) Calculate the sensitivity of the closed-loop input resistance of the series-shunt feedback amplifier with respect to changes in open-loop gain A: (b) Use this formula to estimate the percentage change in closed-loop input resistance if the openloop gain A changes by 10 percent for an amplifier with A = 94 dB and β = 0.01. (c) Calculate the sensitivity of the closed-loop output resistance of the series-shunt feedback amplifier with respect to changes in open-loop gain A: (d) Use this formula to estimate the percentage change in closed-loop output resistance if the openloop gain A changes by 10 percent for an amplifier with A = 100 dB and β = 0.01. 11.6 Transresistance Amplifiers—Shunt-Shunt Feedback
answer: (b) change of Rin for a 10 % change of A
(d) change of Rout for a 10 % change of A
problems.how: Rin = Rid(1 + Aβ), Rout = Ro/(1 + Aβ); differentiate with respect to A.

problems.text: The VTC for an amplifier can be expressed as vo = 15 tanh (1000 vi) V. (a) Use MAT- LAB to find the total harmonic distortion for (a) vi = 0.001 sin 2000πt V. (b) Repeat for vi = 0.002 sin 2000πt V.
problems.how: Fourier series of 15·tanh(1000·vi) found by numerical integration (odd symmetry: only odd harmonics) and checked with an FFT; THD = √(ΣVn²)/V1 up to the 39th harmonic.
assume: The statement asks for MATLAB; the same numbers are computed here with NumPy.

problems.text: A cascade amplifier is to be designed to meet these specifications: Av = 5000 Rin ≥10 MΩ Rout ≤0.1 Ω How many amplifier stages will be required if the stages must use an op amp below? Because of bandwidth requirements, assume that no individual stage can have a gain greater than 50.
problems.how: Total gain is the product of the stage gains: 50ⁿ ≥ 5000 gives n ≥ 2.2 → 3 stages. The Rin and Rout requirements need the op-amp table that the statement refers to (not reproduced in the text).
assume: Only the gain constraint is evaluated here.

problems.text: A 14-bit ADC with VFS = 5.12 V has an output code of 10101110110010. What is the possible range of input voltages?
answer: 3.495 V ≤ vX ≤ 3.496 V (N·LSB ± ½ LSB, N·LSB = 3.496 V)
problems.how: Eq. (12.53) and Fig. 12.28: the quantization error of an ideal ADC is at most ½ LSB.
assume: Range taken as (N ± ½)·LSB as in Fig. 12.28.

problems.text: A 20-bit ADC has VFS = 2 V. (a) What is the value of the LSB? (b) What is the ADC output code for an input voltage of 1.630500 V? (c) What is the ADC output code for an input voltage of 0.997030 V?
problems.how: Code = nearest integer to vX/LSB (quantization error ≤ ½ LSB).

problems.text: A 12-bit counting converter with VFS = 5 V and fc = 1 MHz has an input voltage VX = 3.760 V. (a) What is the output code? What is the conversion time TT for this value of VX if fc = 1 MHz? (b) Repeat for VX = 4.333 V.
problems.how: The counter runs until the DAC output reaches vX: N clock periods, with N = vX/VFS·2¹² truncated (the DAC output must not exceed vX).
assume: Code obtained by truncation (counting converter stops when the DAC output first exceeds vX).

problems.text: A 20-bit dual-ramp converter is to have an integration time T1 = 0.2 s. How rapidly must the unknown and reference voltage switches change state if this timing uncertainty is to be equivalent to less than 0.1 LSB?
problems.how: A timing error ΔT in T1 is a fractional error ΔT/T1 of full scale; 0.1 LSB = 0.1/2²⁰ of full scale.
